summary: The root مري (mry) primarily means to stroke or rub, especially to draw forth milk from a she-camel.

headwords.gloss: The wind draws forth the clouds

parts.t: The wind draws forth the clouds.
(M, TA.) See an ex. in a verse cited voce

headwords.def: الرِّيحُ تَمْرِى السَّحَابَ and The wind draws forth the clouds. (M, TA.) See an ex. in a verse cited voce عَزْلَآءُ .

headwords.gloss: i. q; He disputed with him; did so obstinately

parts.t: [what has been said; not in commencing a disputation]. (Msb.)

headwords.def: مَارَاهُ , inf. n. مُمَارَاةٌ and مِرَآءٌ , i. q. جَادَلَهُ ; (S, K; *) He disputed with him, or did so obstinately, &c.: (TA:) it is only in opposing [what has been said; not in commencing a disputation]. (Msb.)

headwords.gloss: The disputing; contending, together; They two dispute
headwords.def: التَّمَارِى The disputing, or contending, together. (TA.) You say, هُمَا يَتَمَارَيَانِ بِالشِّعْرِ [ They two dispute, or contend, together, with verses or poetry ]. (TA in art. بده .)
اِمْترَى He doubted, به of it. (Kur, xliii. 61.) See 1.
اِسْتَمْرَتِ الإِبِلُ المحَمْضَ for اِسْتَمْرَأَتْهُ : see 1 in art. عدن .
مَرْوٌ A certain plant: see خَافُورٌ , and حَبَقٌ , and فَاخُورٌ .
